claims: A clean CodeRabbit run can never count as `reviewed`, so the closeout re-requests on every clean head: `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:762` (also `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:113`, `cloud-watch-loop.md:49`); `classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal` only returns `reviewed` when there's a PR review record containing `**Run ID**`, and never looks at issue comments for a finished run, so every clean PR and every clean fix push uses one extra paid review round, and state stays at `requested` for good
The new tests don't catch this because they only use review bodies that contain `**Run ID**`; a test is needed for a walkthrough/summary comment covering the current head

Any commenter can suppress the closeout request (minor): `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:774` — the loop over request comments doesn't check who wrote the comment, so anyone can post the marker for the current head, set state to `requested`, and block the real request
The existing Codex request detection has the same gap (doesn't check comment author)

1.why: classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal (pr-ready-state-core.mjs:759-770) returns 'reviewed' only for a CodeRabbit review whose body matches CODERABBIT_REVIEW_RUN_MARKER, and the issue-comment loop (772-784) only looks for request markers, never a finished run. So a run that posts no review record reads as missing/stale, one closeout request goes out per head, and the state then stays 'requested'. That clean runs post only a summary comment is CodeRabbit's behavior and can't be confirmed from the repo.

2.why: The new tests in pr-ready-state.test.mjs (2223-2338) only give review bodies containing '**Run ID**' or empty bodies; no test uses a summary/walkthrough issue comment for the current head, so the gap in claim 1 goes untested.

3.why: The request-comment loop at core.mjs:772-784 never checks the comment author, but this is the known item 'pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772 Trust only authorized closeout requests'.

4.why: The Codex loop (core.mjs:707-731) does skip the author check on request comments, but that code already exists in base (base line 696) and this diff doesn't touch it, so it isn't a defect in this change.
